title: SECOND SPEAKER
statusNote: Published on YouTube; the director supplied the URL on 2026-11-23 (user-confirmed). An old woman teaches a small device the language only she speaks, and the subtitles arrive as it learns; then her granddaughter, who has been practising with it, says hello. Built 2026-11-22 from thirteen takes, all first attempts and all in the cut. Every voice is an ElevenLabs dub (speech-to-speech from each take's guide performance, the device from text) in a language invented for the film and checked against real ones. The director watched draft v1, approved it without notes and authorized the 4K finish; v1-4k is the published master. The description recorded here is the director's edit of the text delivered with the master. Technical checks, approval, finishing authorization and publication are separate events; real-time listening is the director's and is not claimed by the agent. Archived 2026-11-23 under the standard retention: the 4K master, voice stems, references, prompts, timelines, the assembler, delivery records and QA are kept locally; the generated takes are in the private backup; the native draft, the unused alternate-voice cut and derived mixes were removed.

credits.role: Concept, direction, shot planning, image and motion generation, voice casting and dubbing, editing and sound

reviewEvents.evidence: Assembler wrote 1274 frames at 24/1 fps, 1080x1920, bt709 limited range; the frame count was re-read from the encoded file. The delivered soundtrack measured -19.0 LUFS integrated with a sample peak of -1.5 dBFS, and a local transcription of the mix returned the scripted lines in order. Frame pairs at all fifteen boundaries were inspected. Listening and artistic review are not claimed.
The director after watching: “Perfect. Absolutely perfect. Zero notes or edits. 4k upscale please.”

Whole approved master upscaled twofold with the standard model. Decoded 2160x3840, 1274 frames at 24/1 fps, bt709 limited range; audio packets identical to v1; four frames compared with native and one subtitle crop inspected at full size. No real-time playback by the agent.

The director supplied the published YouTube URL on 2026-11-23 after receiving the v1-4k master. Recorded as user-confirmed; the page was not fetched, and the platform date and published text are not independently asserted. The local master hash identifies the delivered file, not the platform transcode.
